title: How Perovskite Solar Cells Are Changing Energy

slides.heading: The Solar Revolution You Haven't Heard Of
slides.body: How perovskite cells are set to make solar power cheaper, lighter, and more efficient than ever before.

slides.heading: What Is Perovskite?
slides.body: Perovskite refers to a crystal structure — ABX₃ — originally found in a Russian mineral. Scientists discovered that synthetic perovskites made from lead, halides, and organic compounds can convert sunlight to electricity with remarkable efficiency.

slides.heading: A Record-Breaking Rise in Efficiency
slides.body: In 2009, perovskite solar cells were just 3.8% efficient. By 2026, they've exceeded 33% in lab conditions — surpassing conventional silicon cells that took decades to reach similar levels. This improvement happened in under 15 years.

slides.heading: Why Silicon Has Limits
slides.body: Traditional silicon solar panels absorb only a portion of the solar spectrum. They require energy-intensive manufacturing at extremely high temperatures. Perovskite can be tuned to absorb different wavelengths and printed at low temperatures using simple processes.

slides.heading: Tandem Cells: The Best of Both Worlds
slides.body: Stacking perovskite on top of silicon creates "tandem" cells that capture more of the solar spectrum. These hybrid cells have demonstrated over 33.9% efficiency — well beyond what either material achieves alone, and approaching the theoretical maximum.

slides.heading: Ultra-Thin and Flexible
slides.body: Unlike rigid silicon panels, perovskite can be deposited as ultra-thin films on flexible substrates. This opens up applications on curved surfaces, vehicle roofs, windows, clothing, and even indoor devices powered by ambient light.

slides.heading: The Durability Challenge
slides.body: Early perovskite cells degraded quickly when exposed to heat, moisture, and light. Researchers are solving this with new chemical compositions, protective coatings, and encapsulation techniques. Commercial-grade durability — 25+ years — is now within reach.

slides.heading: The Lead Problem and Green Alternatives
slides.body: Most high-efficiency perovskites contain lead, raising environmental concerns. Scientists are actively developing tin-based and bismuth-based perovskites as non-toxic alternatives, though they currently lag in efficiency. The race for lead-free versions is accelerating.

slides.heading: From Labs to Rooftops
slides.body: Companies like Oxford PV, Saule Technologies, and several Chinese manufacturers are scaling perovskite production. First commercial perovskite-silicon tandem modules began shipping in 2025, promising panels that generate more electricity per square meter at lower cost.

slides.heading: A Brighter Energy Future
slides.body: Perovskite solar cells could slash the cost of clean electricity and bring solar power to places where conventional panels don't work. The next generation of solar is already here — and it's crystalline, flexible, and shining bright.
